```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Report on 01_rain_vs_flow_figures.R and 02_rain_vs_flow_maps.R. Reads their
# figures and tables only; run both scripts first. Every number in the text
# is computed from their tables.
#
# Inputs:  output/figures/hydro/rain_vs_flow/*.png
#          output/data/hydro/rain_vs_flow/{county_summary,group_summary,
#            seasonal_correlation,seasonal_profile,annual_county,
#            annual_correlation,annual_variance_share,event_ranks,
#            case_timeseries}.csv
# Output:  rain_vs_flow_report.html, next to this file. Figures are embedded,
#          so the file opens on its own in a browser.
# Dependencies: dplyr, readr, tidyr, knitr, rmarkdown (pandoc, no LaTeX)
#
# Render from this folder on Midway:
#   Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("rain_vs_flow_report.Rmd")'

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = "100%")

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
```

```{css, echo = FALSE}
/* Number figures and tables in order ("Figure 1.", "Table 1.") at the start
   of each caption. Figures are numbered through their captions, so every
   figure and table needs one. */
body { counter-reset: figure table; }
.figure .caption::before, figcaption::before {
  counter-increment: figure;
  content: "Figure " counter(figure) ". ";
}
table caption::before {
  counter-increment: table;
  content: "Table " counter(table) ". ";
}
.figure .caption::before, figcaption::before, table caption::before {
  color: #0b0b0b;
  font-weight: bold;
}
/* Light-green label for the figures and tables to show the PI. Wrap a
   chunk in ::: {.pi-highlight} ... ::: to highlight its label. */
.pi-highlight .caption::before, .pi-highlight figcaption::before, .pi-highlight caption::before {
  background-color: #d9f2d0;
  padding: 2px 6px;
}
```

```{r paths}
USER <- Sys.getenv("USER")
source("../../../../../0_utils/paths.R")

fig_dir <- file.path(DIR_FIGURE, "hydro", "rain_vs_flow")
table_dir <- file.path(DIR_REPO_RAINFALL_MORTALITY, "output", "data", "hydro", "rain_vs_flow")
```

```{r read-data}
county <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "county_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
groups <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "group_summary.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))
annual <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "annual_correlation.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))
variance <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "annual_variance_share.csv"), col_types = cols(group = "c"))
annual_county <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "annual_county.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ranks <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "event_ranks.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
seasonal <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "seasonal_correlation.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
profile <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "seasonal_profile.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
case_ts <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "case_timeseries.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Format numbers for the text and tables
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  vapply(x, function(v) format(signif(v, digits), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE), "")
}
fmt_r <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)

group_names <- c("1" = "Low", "2" = "Middle", "3" = "High", "all" = "All counties")

# Drought and flood years: a county's lowest and highest 10% of years. Must
# match extreme_year_share in 01_rain_vs_flow_figures.R.
extreme_year_share <- 0.10

all_counties <- filter(groups, group == "all")
low <- filter(groups, group == "1")
mid <- filter(groups, group == "2")
high <- filter(groups, group == "3")

# Median county value from the annual table, by measure and group ("1", "2",
# "3", "all"); `column` can also be "p10" or "p90"
annual_value <- function(m, g, column = "median") annual[[column]][annual$measure == m & annual$group == g]
annual_r <- function(m, g) fmt_r(annual_value(m, g))
annual_pct <- function(m, g) fmt_pct(annual_value(m, g))

# Low-group counties where rainfall leaves more than half of the flood measure
# unexplained, and whether their flow peaks in a different month (a sign of
# snow, since these counties have little upstream water)
low_flood <- annual_county %>%
  filter(group == 1) %>%
  inner_join(select(county, region_id, peak_shift), by = "region_id") %>%
  mutate(far = unexplained_flood > 0.5)

# Share of the pooled within-county variance of raw annual levels, by group
# ("1", "2", "3", "top 1%") and series ("rain", "flowmean", "flowmax")
variance_pct <- function(g, series) fmt_pct(variance[[series]][variance$group == g])

# Median county correlation by calendar month, for a group ("Low", "Middle", "High")
season_r <- function(g, months) {
  seasonal$corr_median[startsWith(seasonal$label_short, g) & seasonal$cal_month %in% months]
}

# Median county share of the year in one calendar month, as a percentage
profile_pct <- function(g, series, month) {
  sprintf("%.1f", 100 * profile$share_median[
    startsWith(profile$label_short, g) & profile$series == series & profile$cal_month == month
  ])
}

# One row per event and county with rainfall and flow side by side, in the
# order of event_ranks.csv (events as in the figures, counties upstream to
# downstream)
ranks_wide <- ranks %>%
  mutate(series = recode(series, "Rainfall" = "rain", "rainfall_flow" = "flow")) %>%
  select(event, county, series, rank, ratio_to_median, n_years) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = c(rank, ratio_to_median, n_years))

n_flow_higher <- sum(ranks_wide$rank_flow < ranks_wide$rank_rain)
n_tie <- sum(ranks_wide$rank_flow == ranks_wide$rank_rain)

# Rank or ratio to median for one case-study county
rank_of <- function(name, series) ranks_wide[[paste0("rank_", series)]][ranks_wide$county == name]
ratio_of <- function(name, series) {
  sprintf("%.1f", ranks_wide[[paste0("ratio_to_median_", series)]][ranks_wide$county == name])
}

# One county-month in the case time series, relative to the county's mean
# month ("rain" or "flow")
rel_of <- function(name, month, series) {
  sprintf("%.1f", case_ts[[paste0(series, "_rel")]][case_ts$county == name & case_ts$month == month])
}
```

# Summary

In most of the country, flow is the same as rainfall. 
In the top third of counties by upstream ratio (mean flow/mean rainfall), 
it is slightly different, and affects the flood measure (annual max) more 
than the drought measure (annual mean).
From these figures, it looks like rainfal flow captures upstream rainfall 
from outside of county boundaries and the timing of snowmelt.

::: {.pi-highlight}

```{r table-thirds}
# Median county correlation of flow with rainfall, by upstream-ratio third:
# monthly series, drought measures (annual mean) and flood measures (annual
# max), each pair built the same way from the county's monthly series
annual_median <- annual %>%
  filter(measure %in% c("corr_drought", "corr_flood")) %>%
  select(group, measure, median) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = median)

groups %>%
  inner_join(annual_median, by = "group") %>%
  transmute(
    `Upstream-ratio third` = group_names[group],
    Counties = fmt(n_counties, 4),
    `Upstream ratio` = paste0(fmt(ratio_min), " to ", fmt(ratio_max), " (median ", fmt(ratio_median), ")"),
    `Monthly flow vs. monthly rainfall` = fmt_r(corr_median),
    `Drought measure` = fmt_r(corr_drought),
    `Flood measure` = fmt_r(corr_flood)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    align = "lrrrrr",
    caption = paste(
      "Correlation of rainfall_flow with rainfall, median county in each upstream-ratio tertile.",
      "Thirds: counties ranked by upstream ratio (mean flow / mean rainfall)",
      "and split into tertiles. The monthly column is the correlation",
      "over each county's own months. The drought and flood columns are correlations over",
      "each county's years 1950-2025 of the flow and rainfall drought measures (annual mean",
      "of the monthly values) and flood measures (annual max: the biggest monthly value)."
    )
  )
```

:::

**Where they are similar**

- **Counties with little upstream water.** In the low upstream-ratio group,
  the median county correlation is
  `r annual_r("corr_drought", "1")` between the flow and rainfall drought
  measures (annual mean), and `r annual_r("corr_flood", "1")` between the flow
  and rainfall flood measures (annual max). 
- **Month to month, in most of the East and South.** The median county
  correlation of the raw monthly series is
  `r fmt_r(all_counties$corr_median)` (`r fmt_r(low$corr_median)` in the low
  group).

**Where they are different**

- **Along large rivers.** 
- **In snowy regions.** Flow counts snow when it melts, rainfall when it
  falls, so the flood measure picks up the spring melt.
  - In
    `r fmt_pct(mean(low_flood$peak_shift[low_flood$far] != 0))` of them flow
    peaks in a different month from rainfall
    (`r fmt_pct(mean(low_flood$peak_shift[!low_flood$far] != 0))` for the
    rest of the group).

**What flow tells you that rainfall can't**

- **Water from outside the county.** A wet year upstream reaches a
  downstream county even when its own rain is typical.
- **Floods more than droughts.** 

**Flood case studies**

- Four hand-picked flood cases that are known river or rain floods.
- Flow ranks the flood at least as high as rainfall in
    `r n_flow_higher + n_tie` of `r nrow(ranks_wide)` county cases, and
    strictly higher in `r n_flow_higher`.
- Hurricane Harvey, a local-rain flood, ranks first in both which makes sense 
because there's not a lot of upstream water to add. 

# The two variables

**Rainfall** is the precipitation used in the mortality analysis
(`prcp_pop_p1`). It is ERA5-Land `tp_total`: the population-weighted county
mean of daily totals, summed over the month, in mm. It is built by
`era5land_admin/aggregation_scripts/02_aggregate_prcp_temp.py`. 

**rainfall_flow** (`flow_pop`) routes that water downstream. Each grid cell
gets its own rainfall plus the rainfall of every cell upstream of it on a D8
river network (`hydro/coarse/prepflow.py`). The county value is the
population-weighted mean over the county's cells, using the same weights as
rainfall. It is built by `hydro_era5land_admin/01_aggregate_monthly_flow.py`.

# Across geography

```{r fig-maps, fig.cap = "Mean monthly rainfall, mean monthly rainfall_flow, upstream ratio, and correlation of the two monthly series, by county. Lower 48 states."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "1_county_maps.png"))
```

- **Flow and the upstream ratio trace the river network.** 
- **The correlation is close to 1 across most of the East and South.**
- **It is lowest in two kinds of places:**
  - In snowy regions: the interior Pacific Northwest and northern Rockies,
    parts of the Great Basin and central Rockies, and northern New England.
  - Along large rivers, like the lower Mississippi.

```{r fig-where, fig.cap = "Correlation of monthly rainfall and rainfall_flow, and share of flow-extreme months that are not rainfall-extreme, against the upstream ratio."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "2_where_flow_differs.png"))
```

- **Low group (less upstream water): very similar.** The
  median county in the low group has a correlation of
  `r fmt_r(low$corr_median)`. Only `r fmt_pct(low$missed_median)` of its
  flow-extreme months are not rainfall-extreme.
- **High group (high upstream water): the correlation falls and the extremes diverge.** The median
  correlation is `r fmt_r(high$corr_median)`, and
  `r fmt_pct(high$missed_median)` of the months that flow flags as extreme are
  not extreme in local rainfall.
- **Snow outliers.** A few counties have a correlation near or below zero even
  at modest upstream ratios. 

```{r table-groups}
groups %>%
  transmute(
    `Upstream ratio group` = group_names[group],
    Counties = n_counties,
    `Ratio range` = paste(fmt(ratio_min), "to", fmt(ratio_max)),
    `Median county r` = fmt_r(corr_median),
    `Flow extremes missed by rainfall (median county)` = fmt_pct(missed_median),
  ) %>%
  kable(
    align = "lrrrrrr",
    caption = paste(
      "Raw monthly series by upstream-ratio group. County r: one correlation per county.",
      "Flow extremes missed: share of a county's top-5% flow months that are not in its",
      "top-5% rainfall months."
    )
  )
```

# Across time

```{r fig-seasonal, fig.cap = "Correlation of rainfall and rainfall_flow by calendar month, median county in each upstream-ratio group."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "3_seasonal_correlation.png"))
```

- **Low group (little upstream water).**
  - The median correlation is at least
    `r sprintf("%.3f", min(season_r("Low", 5:10)))` from May to October.
  - It falls to `r sprintf("%.3f", season_r("Low", 1))` in January and
    `r sprintf("%.3f", season_r("Low", 2))` in February.
- **High group.**
  - The median correlation is `r fmt_r(min(season_r("High", 1:4)))` to
    `r fmt_r(max(season_r("High", 1:4)))` in January-April, and
    `r fmt_r(min(season_r("High", 5:10)))` to
    `r fmt_r(max(season_r("High", 5:10)))` in May-October.

```{r fig-profile, fig.cap = "Share of the year's rainfall and rainfall_flow in each calendar month, median county in each upstream-ratio group."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "4_seasonal_profile.png"))
```

- The seasonal cycles match where there is little upstream water,
and diverge where there is a lot.
- That fits snow building up over the larger, snowier upstream basins in
    winter and melting in spring.

```{r fig-shift, fig.cap = "Months from the rainfall peak month to the rainfall_flow peak month, by county."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "5_peak_shift_map.png"))
```

# Flood case studies

These cases show whether flow picks up floods that local rainfall
misses. These are four large floods that I hand picked. Each
event has a set of counties, flood months and an expected driver, from the
historical record rather than from data.

- **2011 Missouri River flood** (May-Aug), expected driver upstream flow.
  Burleigh ND, Woodbury IA, Pottawattamie IA, Buchanan MO.
- **2019 Missouri River flood** (Mar-Jun), expected driver upstream flow.
  Dodge NE, Douglas NE, Fremont IA, Holt MO.
- **1993 Great Flood** (Jun-Aug), expected driver both rain and flow.
  Polk IA, Adams IL, St. Charles MO, St. Louis city MO.
- **2017 Hurricane Harvey** (Aug), a contrast case expected to be driven by
  local rain. Fort Bend, Harris, Galveston and Jefferson TX.

::: {.pi-highlight}

```{r fig-timeseries, fig.cap = "Monthly rainfall and rainfall_flow around each flood, each relative to the county's mean month. One example county per event. Shaded: flood months."}
include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, "7_case_timeseries.png"))
```

:::
